candidate.falsifier: A nonpositive LP optimum under a cone means that cone cannot prove the signed threshold, even with exact marginal data.
candidate.mechanism: Replace total-L1 uniformity with exact projections of the actual reflected prime-pair orbit measure to fixed lower moduli before testing whether the signed bad state remains LP-feasible.
candidate.name: lower-modulus marginal cone for q286-WBSS
candidate.prediction: Prime-factor and q286-only projections should still permit synthetic bad arrangements; the full coefficient-support projection family should force positivity because it fixes all lower-modulus components used by the coefficient.
candidate.smallest_test: Stress-select rows from the prior signed-discrepancy receipt by highest lambda and largest L1 load, then solve the minimum-expectation LP under each cone.

decision: Exact lower-modulus marginals sharpen the theorem boundary.  Any cone with a nonpositive LP minimum is too weak as a proof bridge; a positive-forcing cone is only useful if a separate source-backed binary-prime projection theorem can put actual mu_N in that cone.  This separates AP-style projection data from the still-missing signed binary-prime correlation estimate.
selected_target_rule: Union of the top 12 post-discovery rows by lambda and top 6 by L1 worst-case load for each of full and edge-beta in q286-wbss-signed-discrepancy-problem.json.
status_boundary: finite marginal-cone LP falsifier only; no lower-modulus projection theorem, AP theorem, signed discrepancy theorem, q286 threshold theorem, strict-central Goldbach theorem, or Goldbach proof
